ownership_scope: Unjoined StreamLease entries share the same state/capacity checks and generation counter as joined object transfers. Raw legacy batches retain no artificial single-object identity. A client reader retains its Arc through stream return; accepted sink pieces retain it while buffered/pending; each actual write batch clones its proof through the worker call. Empty writes count as retained work even with zero payload. Dropping/cancelling a lane runner does not return a still-live proof. Scope is local client stream/staging/write-call accounting; not universal remote-handler retirement acknowledgement or whole-process RSS.
pressure_scope: Common reservation refusal precedes the lane window/peer slot, plan mutation and reader/writer start, produces no object/source error and schedules a 25 ms readiness retry. Later local admission refusal drops its own common reservation. Each payload is at most 256 KiB; effective share is capped at that payload too, so a wholly stalled first pull cannot take the second background slot. A threshold notification wakes re-pull without waiting for a write/final reply. Retired sink proofs remain until lane credits publish. The historical wire operation and lane window remain compatible. Uploads, inbound classic handlers, old-worker source buffers and all connection/spool resources are not integrated.
historical_window_contract: The previous >=8 MiB payload-occupancy assertion per lane conflicts with the frozen Wave 6 common 8 MiB job/buffer budget and 256 KiB payloads. It is explicitly replaced by >=256 KiB exercised payload and <=512 KiB actual source-read-minus-durable/write plus lane-window occupancy in this one-repository fixture. The original <=16 MiB upper bound, complete identical 24/72 MiB workloads, 60-second completion deadline and two in-flight pulls under link pressure remain. This is a documented resource contract change, not a claim that sustained bulk throughput is unchanged; no ignored historical long qualification is waived.
diagnostics_scope: usage includes joined plus unjoined reservations. joined_usage and stream_usage expose their separate counts/bytes.
